statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-25068: in alsa-lib 1.2.2 to 1.2.15.2, tplg_decode_control_mixer1() in the topology library uses the num_channels field of a binary topology file as a loop bound without checking it against the fixed channel array, so a crafted .tplg file can write past a heap buffer. The fix is https://github.com/alsa-project/alsa-lib/commit/5f7fe33002d2d98d84f72e381ec2cccc0d5d3d40, which rejects the file with "mixer: unexpected channel count". Debian fixed it in trixie in 1.2.14-1+deb13u1 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-25068, Debian bug 1126629). This owner publishes one build, of Debian's 1.2.14-1+deb13u1, in the DHI Debian repository for amd64 and arm64, and that build is the range's fixed version. Its changelog carries Debian's CVE-2026-25068 entry, and its libatopology.so.2 on both architectures contains the "mixer: unexpected channel count" check from that commit. With this range every published build is on the fixed side.
